summary: Master public health risk communication with CERC, WHO RCCE, and infodemic management skills. 5-day hands-on course. Enroll at TrainingCred.com.
lede: Public health risk communication helps professionals share accurate, timely and actionable information during health threats. Designed for mid-career public health professionals who coordinate public messaging, the course builds skills in phased planning, plain-language message design, misinformation response and measuring communication reach and behavioral effects for affected communities.
audienceIntro: This course is built for mid-career public health professionals who are responsible for communicating health risks to the public, coordinating outbreak messaging, or advising health authorities on communication strategy. It assumes you already work within a public health, government health, or humanitarian health system and need to move from ad hoc messaging to structured, evidence-based communication practice.
audience: WHO, UNICEF, or NGO Field Communication Officers
Media and Public Affairs Officers embedded
modules: Foundations of Public Health Risk Communication
Crisis and Emergency Risk Communication Planning
Community Engagement and Vulnerable Population Communication
Media Relations, Spokesperson Skills, and Stakeholder Coordination
prerequisites: Participants should bring a laptop or tablet capable of accessing web-based tools and Google Workspace or equivalent. No specialist software licences are required — all digital tools used in the course are free or open-access. Participants are encouraged to bring a real or recent communication challenge from their own organization to use as a reference scenario during workshop exercises. Basic familiarity with social media platforms (Twitter/X, Facebook, WhatsApp) from a professional communication perspective is helpful but not mandatory.
